topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecturer, outline the lecture series structure, and present the learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Fundamental Concepts and Drivers of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous errors, microenvironmental factors, and inherited risks.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Bad Luck, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between environmental carcinogens and random chance, supported by population-level epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, highlighting the combined roles of EBV and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical compounds directly cause DNA mutations and adducts.

topics.label: Tumour Promoters, Inflammation, and Two-Stage Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors and chronic inflammation act as tumour promoters to drive the expansion of initiated cells.

topics.label: Host Cell Susceptibility and Summary of Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how host developmental timing influences susceptibility to carcinogens, concluding with a recap of carcinogenesis mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, and experimental laboratory methodologies used to detect and evaluate carcinogenic activity.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Decision Making and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks summarize the key takeaways of the lecture and frame cancer prevention around daily risk-benefit evaluations.
